principles: Remove the archived source only after every legacy route and data boundary has one explicit disposition.
Do not reproduce a legacy endpoint when a safer native workflow already answers the operator need.
Do not import legacy consent, learning telemetry or product analytics without a separate lawful purpose and privacy review.
Future native capabilities remain roadmap work but do not require retaining executable legacy source.
No disposition claims scanner production readiness or authorizes live traffic.

route_decisions.rationale: A maintained native CLI, API, Web or SSE workflow covers the operator need without preserving VAP route or payload compatibility.
The legacy surface is outside the offline-first assessment control plane, weakens the native security model, or is replaced by maintained documentation and lifecycle policy.
The user need is valid, but it belongs to an existing native roadmap capability and must not inherit the legacy route, identity or data contract.

data_decisions.rationale: The native state machine preserves partial, timeout and policy-denied outcomes; historical completed records are conservatively imported as partial.
The reviewed snapshot, verification, plan, approval and idempotent terminal import chain preserves historical provenance without creating executable work.
Native audit is authoritative and redacted; searchable audit and stronger evidence integrity remain native roadmap work, while legacy personal-data-rich audit is not imported.
Vulcan owns native versioned reports; further browser delivery must reuse it rather than retain legacy report files or routes.
Native cancellation and recovery are verified; live Celery identifiers are deliberately never converted into native executable work.

remaining_sec_a_work: worker concurrency bounds independent from the shared API/Web request gate
physical removal of the archived VAP source and stale source-dependent documentation
